analysis:
Examined base-side units of ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift (lines 552-1671) along with the patch map.

Head changes visible in the patch:
- Line 207 replaces autopilotAllowsModel with autopilotServesModel in the load guard. The guard still also admits an explicit matching autopilot command.
- transitionGenerations.begin(.modelLoading) is added at head 397 and 434.
- reconcileAutopilotPlacements() is called after slot removal in unloadModel (head 1148-1150).
- There are further changes near head 1298-1306, around evictableModelSlots. Their content was not fully supplied (the patch excerpt is truncated).

Security relevance:
- These are availability and scheduling changes: autopilot selection, transition generation tracking and eviction eligibility.
- They do not touch the weight-hash TOCTOU bracketing (base 604-641) or cacheEligibleWeightHash gating for the SSD prefix cache (T-041 binding to a verified weightHash).
- They do not touch attestation, encryption, App Attest authorization (TB-011/T-053), or loadedModelHashesSnapshot reporting.
- No plaintext or crypto path changed.

Integration questions for the next pass:
- Semantics of autopilotServesModel vs autopilotAllowsModel. If it is narrower or broader, it changes which models can be loaded on request. This is a local availability/policy question, not authorization, since the coordinator controls advertisement.
- The head 1298-1306 evictableModelSlots changes. Confirm they do not allow evicting slots with in-flight requests, which would be a DoS within T-010/T-029 scope. A wrong eviction gate would also only fail within the provider's own process.
- Whether transitionGenerations.begin is balanced on every catch path. Base catch paths 963-1015 must end the generation; otherwise loads could wedge (availability).

No concrete regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
